title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' notes (Grothendieck's own pagination 501; archive p. 399). The likely setting is G = GL_2 and SG = SL_2. T_0 ≅ G_m is the centre. T_ρ and T_σ are maximal tori of G attached to two elements ρ, σ, and N'_σ is (part of) the normalizer of T_σ. The group M_{ρ,σ} is defined as G*_{ρ,σ}(0)·SG, a semidirect product inside (T_0×T_ρ×N'_σ)·SG. It is presumably a symmetry group of the space of (ρ,σ)-type solutions of the loop equation, i.e. pairs of GL_2-matrices satisfying the loop relation.

On the previous page Grothendieck says he is overcomplicating things. He decides first to describe the neutral component M°.

Step (15): the component group is M/M° ≅ G*(0)/G*(0)° ≅ μ_2×μ_2, citing p.489 (23). Hence M° = G*(0)°·SG ⊂ (T_0×T_ρ×T_σ)·SG. Since T_ρ and T_σ act trivially on SG, this is ≅ T_ρ×T_σ×(T_0·SG), and T_0·SG = G_m·SL_2 = GL_2 = G.

Step (16): M° embeds in T_ρ×T_σ×G as {(x,y,f) | det x = det y = det f}. Dimension check: 2+2+4−2 = 6.

Step (17): J° := Ker(M° → PG = G/G_m). Here f must be a scalar λ, giving {(x,y,λ) | det x = det y = λ²}, a 3-dimensional torus. He identifies it with T_ρ ×_{G_m} T_σ = {(x,y) | det x = det y} and with SG*(0)°.

Step (18): I° := Ker(M° → G) is f = 1, giving ST_ρ×ST_σ (det x = det y = 1).

The page ends 'Récapitulons'. The next page states the resulting theorem: M is an extension of μ_2×μ_2 by M°, and there is an exact sequence 1 → ST_ρ×ST_σ → M° → G → 1, with central subgroups.

This is a routine structural computation of a specific algebraic group in Grothendieck's study of the loop equation (Teichmüller/Galois–Teichmüller context of La Longue Marche).
errors: (17): the natural projection (x,y,λ) ↦ (x,y) from {det x = det y = λ²} onto T_ρ×_{G_m}T_σ is not an isomorphism. It is a degree-2 isogeny with kernel {(1,1,−1)} ≅ μ_2. Both are connected 3-dimensional tori: the character-lattice relations (1,1,0,0,−2), (0,0,1,1,−2) span a saturated sublattice. So they are abstractly isomorphic, but the '≃' is not justified by the evident map. It also does not respect the quotients by ST_ρ×ST_σ, where λ ↦ λ² appears. A crossed-out '≃ T_ρ×_{G_m}T_σ' on the same line suggests Grothendieck himself hesitated here.
Minor: '≃ T_ρ×T_σ×(T_0·SG)' presupposes that the semidirect product action of T_ρ×T_σ on SG is trivial; this holds in context but is not stated on this page.

ideas.what: Determination of the component group μ_2×μ_2 and the neutral component of the symmetry group M_{ρ,σ} as a fibre-product subgroup of T_ρ×T_σ×GL_2 cut out by equal determinants
ideas.modern_name: structure of a disconnected algebraic group (neutral component, π_0) built from tori and SL_2
ideas.where_published: Not known in published form; part of the unpublished 'équation des lacets' manuscripts

ideas.what: Kernels of M° → PGL_2 (a torus T_ρ×_{G_m}T_σ, up to isogeny) and of M° → GL_2 (ST_ρ×ST_σ)
ideas.modern_name: fibre products of tori over G_m via det; norm-one subtori

deep.surprise_reason: A routine (and slightly sloppy: an isogeny is written as an isomorphism) computation of the structure of an auxiliary algebraic group inside a long private calculation. There are no new ideas or connections on the page itself.
transcription_corrections: Top number '501' is Grothendieck's own pagination; the archive page number is 399 (bottom left).
The insertion above 'le groupe' is barely legible; 'commutatif' is uncertain.
In (17), the second line contains a struck-through attempted identification with T_ρ×_{G_m}T_σ (over the 'G/G_m' annotation); the transcription's bracketed deletion is roughly right.
'Donc le noyau[?]' is closer to 'Dans le noyau'/'D'où le noyau' (illegible); the meaning is the kernel J°.
